tema: Studies muscle fibre conduction velocity using surface EMG in women with CFS and fibromyalgia.
diseno: Surface EMG study of the biceps brachii under static load; sample size not stated in the available text.
hallazgos: In women with CFS, conduction velocity increases abnormally with moderate force, suggesting hyperactivated muscle membranes in high-threshold motor units; in fibromyalgia the hyperactivity mainly affects low-threshold tonic units.
conclusion: The muscle membranes of the force-generating units behave abnormally in CFS, with a possible contribution of central neural dysregulation, which helps explain symptoms and mechanisms.
triangulacion: The abstract is opening text (header and highlights), but agrees with the keywords and with the PDF conclusions, which develop the difference between CFS and fibromyalgia.

tema: Proposes that ME/CFS is due to a breakdown of homeostasis with an altered set point that maintains a dysfunctional state.
diseno: Theoretical article without collection of new data.
hallazgos: The theory proposes that homeostasis persistently pushes the organism toward a pathological state because the imbalance is not restored, with endocrine and immune changes; it receives tentative support from mitochondrial dysfunction and from data on thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) in cancer-related fatigue.
conclusion: The breakdown of the homeostatic restoring function is a plausible theory; randomized trials with TRH would be useful, although the approach is speculative.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions are more cautious and stress the speculative nature and the need for research before drawing conclusions.

tema: Compares the plasma metabolic signatures of ME/CFS patients and controls in a discovery cohort.
diseno: Pilot case-control study: 17 patients and 15 matched controls, all women; plasma metabolomics by mass spectrometry (361 metabolites) and pathway analysis.
hallazgos: 74 metabolites differed (P<0.05) and 35 after correction (Q<0.15), including energy compounds. The most affected pathways were taurine metabolism, glycerophospholipids, primary bile acids and glyoxylate/dicarboxylate, linked to fatty acid metabolism; also purines (ADP, ATP), pyrimidines, amino acids, glucose and oxaloacetate.
conclusion: Metabolomics implicates lipid metabolism, not previously linked to ME/CFS; the pilot study requires verification in a larger cohort.
triangulacion: The three sources agree on the lipid focus. The conclusions (with methods noise) are more cautious than the abstract and stress the pilot nature of the study.

tema: Determines the frequency and correlates of SEID/CFS in patients at a sleep unit with hypersomnolence.
diseno: Retrospective pilot study with 187 hypersomnolent patients (idiopathic hypersomnia, narcolepsy type 2, sleepiness after apnoea treatment, short sleep, normal study); questionnaires, clinical records and polysomnography.
hallazgos: 21% met SEID criteria, with no differences between sleep diagnoses, sex, age, Epworth, depression or sleep parameters. The SEID group had deeper fatigue and lower response to wake-promoting drugs (88.6% versus 67.7%).
conclusion: SEID is a frequent comorbidity in hypersomnolence, not specific to a subtype, which may predict a worse response to treatment.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent, although the focus is sleep rather than exercise. The discussion adds caution: retrospective design, absence of a validated SEID questionnaire and need for prospective validation.

tema: Compares the level of sickness behaviour in ME/CFS and chronic pain with that of experimental inflammation and other populations.
diseno: Cross-sectional study with the SicknessQ questionnaire in six samples: ME/CFS (38), chronic pain (190), healthy with LPS (29), primary care (163), general population (155) and healthy (48); linear and moderated regression.
hallazgos: SicknessQ scores: LPS 16.3, ME/CFS 16.1 and chronic pain 16.1, higher than primary care (10.7), general population (5.4) and healthy (3.6). Greater sickness behaviour was associated with worse self-perceived health, although less so in ME/CFS and chronic pain.
conclusion: Patients with ME/CFS and chronic pain report sickness behaviour comparable to experimental inflammation; studying immune-brain interactions is justified.
triangulacion: Coherence between keywords and abstract; the conclusions (discussion) are mostly noise (funding, contributions) and only reinforce research into sickness behaviour circuits.

tema: Identifies the experiences and attitudes of people with ME regarding pacing with a heart rate monitor (HRM).
diseno: International online survey of 40 questions disseminated on websites and social media; 488 people with ME, mostly women aged 35-50 with more than 5 years of illness.
hallazgos: More than 100 types of monitor were used and more than 30 benefits and more than 30 drawbacks were identified; participants reported that the HRM reduced the severity of ME and the severity and duration of PEM.
conclusion: The HRM helps to understand and manage PEM and to increase activities, including work; more research and training of professionals in its safe use are needed.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The conclusions add as a drawback a possible initial reduction in physical function and acknowledge sample limitations; the benefits are self-reported.

tema: Describes the design and community recruitment of DecodeME, a large genetic study of ME/CFS in the UK.
diseno: Study protocol co-produced by people with lived experience and scientists; recruitment of up to 25,000 people with a clinical diagnosis of ME/CFS (≥16 years), including 5,000 post SARS-CoV-2 infection; questionnaires and saliva DNA by post; GWAS against UK Biobank controls.
hallazgos: There are no genetic results; digital marketing and social media led 29,000 people with ME/CFS to pre-register, and postal sample sending facilitates participation of the most severely affected.
conclusion: The GWAS should generate hypotheses about the genes, mechanisms and cell types involved; the data will be disseminated as variants, genomic intervals and summary statistics in open-access publications.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract are consistent on community recruitment, GWAS and COVID-19; the conclusions (from the discussion) are only noise about consent, conflicts of interest and editorial advertising, providing no content.

tema: Investigates HPA axis function in CFS using the combined dexamethasone/CRF test, considering early life stress.
diseno: Case-control study with 34 women with CFS and 25 healthy controls; low-dose Dex/CRF test with salivary cortisol; early life stress assessed with a structured interview; exclusion of current major depression.
hallazgos: Cortisol responses after dexamethasone were lower in patients before and after CRF. Excluding those taking oral oestrogens, patients without early life stress showed lower responses than those with it and than controls.
conclusion: CFS is globally associated with lower cortisol responses on the Dex/CRF test, an effect clear only in patients without early life stress, which supports increased glucocorticoid feedback and/or lower central drive of the HPA axis.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the structured abstract) are consistent and the conclusion is identical; the influence of oestrogens appears only in the secondary analysis.

tema: Documents the effect of prolonged intravenous saline administration on cardiopulmonary function and symptoms in an ME/CFS patient.
diseno: Case study of a 38-year-old woman who received 1 L of 0.9% saline via central line for 675 days; periodic CPETs and open-ended questionnaire on symptoms and recovery.
hallazgos: VO2, HR and systolic BP at peak and VAT improved; the recovery time after CPET fell from 5 days to 1-2 days, with better quality of life and capacity for daily activities.
conclusion: IV saline could have beneficial effects on cardiopulmonary function and symptoms, which should be studied in larger randomized trials.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions are cautious (exploratory single-case study) and add the advantage of few adverse effects against the invasiveness of the route.

tema: Determines the statistical properties (reliability and responsiveness to change) of CPET measures in ME/CFS.
diseno: Study with 51 women with ME/CFS and 10 similar sedentary women; two CPETs 24 h apart; ANOVA, Cohen's d, ICC, MDC95 and coefficients of variation.
hallazgos: The measures showed moderate to high reliability in ME/CFS and moderate to large effect sizes versus controls; the MDC95 was generally greater in ME/CFS and the coefficients of variation were comparable.
conclusion: CPET measures have adequate responsiveness to change and reproducibility for clinical and research applications.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract and agree with it and with the keywords. Nuance: the reliability described contrasts with other studies in the batch that highlight the lack of reproducibility on the second CPET.

tema: Develops and evaluates the measurement properties of the PAQ questionnaire on daily activities affected by PEM/PESE.
diseno: Psychometric study with an online survey adapted from the Patient-Specific Functional Scale; 981 responses (675 complete); test-retest with ICC, MDC95 and ceiling/floor effects.
hallazgos: Test-retest reliability was acceptable to excellent depending on function and scale; the MDC95 indicated responsiveness to change and ceiling and floor effects were infrequent.
conclusion: The PAQ is valid, reliable and sensitive; its mapping to the WHO ICF facilitates its integration into medical records, although rarely selected functions require further study.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The conclusions add the integration with the ICF and warn of low power for rarely chosen functions; the keywords include long COVID.

tema: Develops a clinical prediction rule to identify PEM from a few symptoms after a two-day CPET.
diseno: Study with 49 ME/CFS patients and 10 healthy sedentary individuals; two maximal CPETs 24 h apart; symptoms at five time points classified into 19 categories; Fisher and ROC analysis.
hallazgos: At all time points, at most two symptoms were enough to differentiate groups, and just one a week after the second CPET. Fatigue, cognitive dysfunction, lack of positive mood and decreased function were consistent predictors.
conclusion: Asking about post-exertional cognitive dysfunction, functional decline and lack of positive mood can identify PEM quickly and accurately; it requires validation in larger samples.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent. The PDF conclusions are more assertive than the abstract in omitting the need for validation in larger samples.

tema: Seeks to separate the brain networks associated with fatigue and pain in ME/CFS and link their changes to clinical improvement after cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT).
diseno: Resting-state fMRI before and after CBT versus waiting list; analysis of fronto-parietal, premotor, somatomotor and DMN networks. The sample size appears truncated (only one group of 29 is stated).
hallazgos: Fatigue was associated with greater SMN-PMN connectivity and lower SMN-DMN, and pain with lower PMN-DMN. CBT improved SMN-DMN connectivity versus waiting list, and clinical improvement was associated with increased frontal SMN-DMN connectivity.
conclusion: The results provide information on dissociable neural mechanisms of fatigue and pain and their modification by CBT in successfully treated patients; more research is needed to individualize treatments.
triangulacion: The conclusions come from the abstract, so they agree by construction; keywords and abstract are consistent. The abstract's methods are truncated.

tema: Reviews emerging neurological and immunological biomarkers of CFS and their potential to define subtypes and guide treatment.
diseno: Narrative review. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Classifies reliable but scattered markers into categories to delimit aetiologically distinct subtypes, taking the phenotyping of chronic prostatitis/chronic pelvic pain as a model.
conclusion: Biomarkers could characterize subgroups by phenotype, prognosis and therapeutic response, but criteria must be defined, validated and tested against sick controls to assess their specificity.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions agree; the conclusions add specific methodological requirements (sick controls with comorbidities, validation) absent from the abstract.

tema: Presents the persistent antigen hypothesis, linked to HLA-antigen incongruence, as the basis of Gulf War illness, long COVID and ME/CFS.
diseno: Hypothesis-oriented review on the role of HLA in the immune response to foreign antigens. No sample stated.
hallazgos: Health outcomes after exposure to foreign antigens depend on the host immune system and in particular on its HLA composition; lack of HLA protection would allow the persistence of antigens that cause chronic damage in the brain and other organs.
conclusion: Eliminating persistent antigens could relieve symptoms; therapeutic plasma exchange would be most useful in Gulf War illness and only temporary in latent viruses.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and discussion are consistent; the discussion adds the therapeutic proposal of plasma exchange, absent from the abstract, and acknowledges its risks and cost.

tema: Popular blog post (Health Rising) on 'phantom nasal congestion' and mid-facial pain in ME/CFS and fibromyalgia.
diseno: Popular article summarizing the research of James Baraniuk (1998-2012); no own study.
hallazgos: Sinus pain and non-allergic rhinitis would affect about 50% of people with ME/CFS, with more mid-facial pain than in allergic rhinitis or rhinosinusitis, but without evidence of inflammation or obstruction; analgesics, antibiotics and nasal corticosteroids are usually ineffective.
conclusion: Not stated.
triangulacion: Only the opening text is available; there are no keywords or conclusions, so triangulation is not possible.

tema: Analyses the use of person-first versus identity-first language to refer to people with ME/CFS in medical research.
diseno: Content analysis of 85 medical research articles in English; 3211 references coded.
hallazgos: Identity-first language predominated (61.9%), followed by person-first (22.9%) and other descriptors (15.2%); 72.9% of the articles used both forms.
conclusion: Identity-first language predominates in the literature; documenting it contributes to the debate on representation and inclusion in scientific communication.
triangulacion: High coherence. The PDF conclusions are more cautious: they acknowledge a non-representative sample and that patient preferences were not assessed, so the link with stigma (present in the keywords) is speculative.

tema: Examines the relationship between hours of upright activity and orthostatic intolerance in ME/CFS as an accessible clinical tool.
diseno: Study with 25 women with ME/CFS and 25 matched healthy controls; self-recording of hours of upright activity (HUA) and OI questionnaires; analysis by groups of <5 and ≥5 HUA and by employment status (ANOVA).
hallazgos: Patients had fewer HUA, worse symptoms and OI interference. Those with <5 HUA had more severe OI symptoms; only 33% worked, all from the ≥5 HUA group.
conclusion: Recording HUA and assessing OI with standardized instruments can be useful for the diagnosis, treatment and management of ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the abstract) are consistent and reinforce the usefulness of simple clinical tools and the occupational impact of OI.

tema: Tests the hypothesis that POTS patients have functional autoantibodies against adrenergic receptors.
diseno: Study with 14 POTS patients from two institutions and 10 healthy subjects; contractility assay in rat cremaster arterioles and cell assays with transfected receptors for β1AR, β2AR and α1AR.
hallazgos: All POTS sera showed α1AR-mediated arteriolar contractile activity, acted as partial α1AR antagonists and increased β1AR activation; a subgroup had greater β2AR activity, with specific binding to the three receptors.
conclusion: Partial antagonist α1AR autoantibodies, together with agonist β1AR and β2AR autoantibodies, would explain the compensatory sympathetic activation and excessive tachycardia in POTS.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions (from the abstract) are consistent and reinforce an autoimmune basis of POTS; the study does not include ME/CFS patients.

tema: Compares machine learning classification of CFS patients based on structural MRI versus that based on self-reports.
diseno: Study with T1 MRI in 18 patients and 15 controls; FreeSurfer segmentation of 61 a priori regions and visual analogue scales; linear support vector machine with bootstrap correction.
hallazgos: The MRI model reached an accuracy of 79.58% and the self-report model 95.95%; areas related to cognition, emotion and memory contributed.
conclusion: Structural MRI abnormalities serve to discriminate CFS from controls, but self-reports remain more effective in classification.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and conclusions are consistent; the conclusions highlight the high MRI accuracy and the possible pathogenic usefulness, with a somewhat more optimistic tone than the abstract.

tema: Proposes a neuroinflammatory paradigm in which a compromised hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus (PVN) would explain the pathophysiology of ME/CFS.
diseno: Hypothesis article based on literature (inflammatory marker and PET/MRI studies). No sample stated.
hallazgos: Chronic and fluctuating neuroinflammation of the PVN would alter its threshold for processing stress signals, explaining hypersensitivity to stressors, PEM and relapses; triggers such as viruses, toxins or trauma could affect the PVN, and limbic-hypothalamic-autonomic dysfunction would explain the diversity of symptoms.
conclusion: The authors hope that a more sensitive diagnostic brain signature by MRI will allow neuroinflammation to be identified in ME/CFS.
triangulacion: Keywords and abstract agree fully; the discussion contributes little (a wish for a diagnostic MRI signature) along with acknowledgements and declarations of the authors' personal experience with the disease.

tema: Compares symptoms after a two-day CPET between ME/CFS patients and healthy controls.
diseno: Study with 49 ME/CFS patients and 10 controls; open-ended questionnaires at five time points after two maximal CPETs 24 h apart; 19 symptom categories.
hallazgos: Patients reported a mean of 14 symptoms versus 4 in controls, and 4 during the following seven days versus none in controls. Fatigue, cognitive dysfunction and sleep problems were the most frequent; the greatest differences were in cognitive dysfunction, decline in function and positive feelings.
conclusion: A standardized exertion stimulus produces prolonged and diverse symptoms in ME/CFS, useful for improving the diagnosis and treatment of PEM.
triangulacion: The three sources agree. The PDF conclusions add that recovery is bimodal, that the CPET does not appear to cause permanent harm and applications for occupational therapy.

tema: According to the title, deals with the modulation of beta-adrenergic autoantibodies over time in post-viral ME/CFS.
diseno: Not stated.
hallazgos: Not stated.
conclusion: Not stated.
triangulacion: There are no keywords, abstract or conclusions available; only the title, so it is not possible to triangulate or to classify the type of document with certainty.

tema: Reviews (a 'state-of-the-art' JACC review) the cardiovascular alterations associated with ME/CFS.
diseno: Narrative review.
hallazgos: Patients frequently have reduced stroke volume, with an inverse relationship between cardiac output and PEM severity; MRI shows reduced stroke, end-systolic and end-diastolic volumes and wall mass. Reduced nocturnal blood pressure, orthostatic tachycardia and/or hypocapnia are also described, as well as the usefulness of two consecutive CPETs to objectify PEM.
conclusion: Changes such as lower stroke volume and cardiac output, lower total blood volume and altered HRV with postural hypotension could contribute to symptoms; their relationship to fatigue and PEM and the role of deconditioning remain to be clarified.
triangulacion: The three sources are consistent; the 'abstract' is the opening text that contains the summary. The PDF conclusions are more cautious and introduce deconditioning as an open question.

tema: Presents mapMECFS, a data portal for sharing and integrating molecular datasets on ME/CFS across disciplines and centres.
diseno: Development of a portal based on the open-source CKAN framework by the NIH-funded ME/CFS Data Management and Coordinating Center, with metadata collection, intelligent search and domain-agnostic data integration.
hallazgos: The portal allows molecular datasets to be explored, shared, compared and downloaded in a single repository, with curated data from public repositories, peer-reviewed publications and members of the ME/CFS Research Network.
conclusion: mapMECFS is a disease-specific portal, accessible with registration and designed according to the FAIR principles, which seeks to improve collaboration and continues to be expanded with systems biology methods.
triangulacion: Keywords, abstract and PDF conclusions are fully consistent on data integration, discoverability and reuse; the conclusions add the reference to the FAIR principles and the invitation to users.
